title: Machine for Comparing Records
statement: For every natural number $k$ and finite decidable state types $Q$ and $T$, there are a finite decidable state type $P$, a deterministic two-work-tape machine $R$ over the record alphabet, distinct states $\mathrm{yes},\mathrm{no}\in P$, designated entry state, and constant $C$ such that the following holds. For any input string, lists of fields $f,g$ each having exactly $k+3$ fields, and initial configuration $d$ in the entry state whose two work tapes encode $f$ and $g$ at their respective head positions, the machine reaches the original configuration with only its state changed to $\mathrm{yes}$ if $f=g$, and to $\mathrm{no}$ otherwise, in some time $t\le C(|\langle f\rangle|+1)$. Before time $t$ it visits neither decision state, and through time $t$ each work-tape head stays within distance $C(|\langle f\rangle|+1)$ of its starting position; here $\langle f\rangle$ denotes the concatenation of the fields of $f$ with blank separators, and the tape encodings agree with that concatenation at offsets from $-1$ through its length (and likewise for $g$).
hypotheses_covered: Two lists of fields each of length $k+3$
Initial configuration in the designated entry state
The two work-tape record encodings hold at offsets $-1$ through the joined record length
